purpose: Reference extraction field meanings. Apply only to selected fields. The selected schema defines allowed shapes and fragment forms; use only supplied reference IDs.
kind: Use claims when source facts or exact-token obligations exist. Meaningful prose requires claims; claims may be empty only when there are exact-token obligations but no prose facts to extract. Use no_feature_claim with a reason only when neither exists.
claims: One independently meaningful source fact per entry. Include meaningful identity and purpose headings. Keep each fact's conditions, qualifiers, obligation strength and required literal text; separate independent behavior, implementation and verification facts. Do not invent facts.
content: The meaning of this one claim. Classify by what the source requires or states, not keywords or obligation strength.

content.kind.business: Feature identity, purpose, goals or observable product behavior, including outputs, conditions and behavioral constraints. Preserve technical qualifiers with the behavior.
content.kind.design: An explicit design decision or constraint.
content.kind.technical: Source-stated implementation mechanisms, dependencies, runtime environments, interfaces or protocols. Technical terminology alone does not make observable behavior technical.
content.kind.validation: An explicit obligation to test, inspect, measure or otherwise verify correctness. A behavioral requirement being testable does not make it a validation claim.
content.kind.implementation_assumption: An assumption stated by the source, never an invented default.
content.kind.open_question: A question left unresolved by the source.
content.kind.scope_guard: An explicit inclusion, exclusion or scope boundary.

segments: Ordered fragments concatenated into one claim, not separate claims. Prefer one complete string unless a permitted reference is needed. References insert supplied display values; strings express meaning.
nodes: Ordered fragments concatenated into one reference text. Prefer one complete string unless a permitted reference is needed. References insert supplied display values; strings express meaning.
citations: Source evidence for the complete claim, including its conditions. Each first/last pair selects an inclusive range of source_lines IDs from the current input.
